name: Accelerate (BLAS and LAPACK)
baseline: Unoptimized Linpack code (no tuned BLAS); Eigen for single-precision GEMM
one_liner: Apple's tuned BLAS and LAPACK; Linpack over 24x faster than untuned code and SGEMM about 2.5x faster than Eigen on iPhone XS.

name: Accelerate (vDSP and vForce element-wise math)
baseline: Plain Swift for loops and map over [Double] and [Float]
one_liner: Apple's vectorized array math; claimed 3-10x over scalar loops, but optimized Swift loops match it on simple element-wise arithmetic.

name: vImage (vImageScale_ARGB8888)
baseline: UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing a UIImage(contentsOfFile:) into a smaller context
one_liner: Accelerate's SIMD image scaler; resizing a JPEG from disk was 16x slower than UIGraphicsImageRenderer in an iPhone 7 test.

name: Compression framework (LZ4)
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB and NSData.compressed(using: .zlib)
one_liner: Apple's LZ4 codec; upstream LZ4 decompresses 12.9x and compresses 6.2x faster than zlib's fastest level, with larger output.

name: Compression framework (LZFSE)
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB (zlib level 5) and NSData.compressed(using: .zlib)
one_liner: Apple's LZFSE matches zlib's ratio while compressing 3.4x and decompressing 2.3x faster in an independent benchmark.

name: Compression framework (LZMESH)
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB and COMPRESSION_LZFSE
one_liner: Apple's OS 27 general-purpose codec, documented as decoding 3.5x faster than zlib with a better ratio than zlib or LZFSE.

name: Compression framework (LZRAVEN)
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_LZMA (NSData.compressed(using: .lzma))
one_liner: Apple's OS 27 high-ratio codec, documented as decoding 3x faster than LZMA at a similar or slightly better ratio.

name: Core AI (LLM runtime, Core ML successor)
baseline: Core ML LLM conversions on the Neural Engine (CoreML-LLM), and MLX Swift as the fastest third-party alternative
one_liner: Apple's Core ML successor in iOS 27/macOS 27; decodes LLMs several times faster than Core ML conversions and ties MLX on dense models.

name: Core Data (used directly instead of SwiftData)
baseline: SwiftData @Model objects (iOS 17)
one_liner: Using Core Data directly skips SwiftData's model layer; developers report fetches about 20x faster, but only anecdotally.

name: Core Image (CILanczosScaleTransform)
baseline: UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing a UIImage(contentsOfFile:) into a smaller context
one_liner: Core Image's Lanczos scale filter; resizing a JPEG from disk was about 17.6x slower than UIGraphicsImageRenderer on an iPhone 7.

name: Core ML stateful models (KV cache as model state)
baseline: Core ML LLM with the key-value cache passed as model inputs and outputs (the pre-macOS 15 / iOS 18 pattern)
one_liner: Core ML states keep an LLM's KV cache inside the model, decoding about 13x faster than passing the cache as inputs at 2K context.

name: Foundation Base64 (swift-foundation 2025 rewrite)
baseline: Foundation base64EncodedString / Data(base64Encoded:) as shipped before February 2025
one_liner: Foundation's own Base64, rewritten in Swift in 2025: 1 MB encodes and decodes 5-7.5x faster than the version it replaced.

name: Date.FormatStyle (Swift Foundation, macOS 14 / iOS 17)
baseline: Date.FormatStyle on macOS 13 / iOS 16 (Objective-C Foundation)
one_liner: Apple reports a 150% speedup for Date.FormatStyle template formatting after Foundation's Swift rewrite in macOS 14 and iOS 17.

name: Date.ISO8601FormatStyle (Swift Foundation, ICU-free)
baseline: Date.ISO8601FormatStyle formatting on the earlier ICU-backed implementation
one_liner: Swift Foundation rebuilt ISO 8601 formatting on its own Gregorian calendar, cutting ICU out and formatting about 4.3x faster.

name: Foundation JSONDecoder / JSONEncoder (swift-foundation rewrite)
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder before macOS 14 / iOS 17 (Swift wrapper over NSJSONSerialization)
one_liner: Apple's 2023 Swift rewrite of JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder; 2x-5x faster decoding than the NSJSONSerialization-based version it replaced.

name: NSRegularExpression (vs Swift Regex)
baseline: Swift Regex (Regex literals and Regex(String), Swift 5.7 to 6.3)
one_liner: Foundation's ICU regex is ~19x cheaper to construct than Swift Regex and avoids some backtracking cliffs; matching is near parity once cached.

name: Image I/O (CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex)
baseline: UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing a full UIImage(contentsOfFile:) into a smaller context
one_liner: ImageIO's thumbnail call cuts decode memory by about 10x, but timed no faster than UIGraphicsImageRenderer in an iPhone 7 test.

name: os_unfair_lock (os framework)
baseline: DispatchQueue.sync on a serial queue used as a mutex; also pthread_mutex, which NSLock wraps
one_liner: Apple's unfair lock: about 29x faster than DispatchQueue.sync and 1.4x faster than pthread_mutex in an uncontended loop.

name: OSAllocatedUnfairLock (os framework)
baseline: NSLock
one_liner: Heap-allocated Swift wrapper for os_unfair_lock; faster than NSLock uncontended, but measured 1.75x slower under heavy contention.

name: SwiftUI List (macOS 26)
baseline: SwiftUI List on macOS 15 and earlier
one_liner: Apple says SwiftUI List on macOS 26 loads 100,000+ item lists 6x faster and updates them up to 16x faster than before.

name: SwiftUI List (vs ScrollView + LazyVStack)
baseline: SwiftUI ScrollView containing a LazyVStack
one_liner: In a 1,000-row image stress test on iOS 17.5, SwiftUI List scrolled 9.5x faster than LazyVStack with far fewer hangs.

name: Synchronization.Mutex (Swift 6)
baseline: NSLock, or an actor used as a lock
one_liner: Swift 6's cross-platform lock; 1.6x faster than NSLock and 7.3x faster than an actor in one debug-build test.

name: Auto Layout (iOS 12 engine)
baseline: Auto Layout on iOS 11
one_liner: The iOS 12 Auto Layout engine ran 1.22x faster than iOS 11's on the same iPhone 7, narrowing but not closing the gap to frame layout.

name: TextKit 2 (NSTextLayoutManager)
baseline: TextKit 1 (NSLayoutManager) in UITextView and NSTextView
one_liner: Apple's viewport-based text engine; pitched as faster than TextKit 1 for large documents, but no published numbers and mixed field reports.

name: Xcode compilation cache (COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING, Xcode 26)
baseline: xcodebuild clean build with no cache
one_liner: Xcode 26's opt-in content-addressed compilation cache; Tuist measured 18-77% shorter clean builds once the cache is warm.

name: Explicitly built modules (Xcode 16+)
baseline: Implicitly built Clang and Swift modules (Xcode 15 and earlier)
one_liner: Xcode 16's explicit module builds: faster LLDB startup is measured, but independent tests found clean builds slower.

name: ld-prime (Xcode 15+ linker)
baseline: ld64, Apple's linker in Xcode 14 and earlier (Chromium's comparison is against LLD, which beat ld64)
one_liner: Apple's rewritten linker, default since Xcode 15: up to 5x faster than ld64 per Apple, and 4-6x faster than LLD in Chromium's builds.

name: lottie-ios (Core Animation rendering engine)
baseline: Lottie's Main Thread rendering engine (the only engine before 3.4.0, default before 4.0)
one_liner: Lottie's default iOS renderer since 4.0: plays animations as CAAnimations in the render server instead of redrawing on the main thread each frame.

name: LASwift
baseline: Plain Swift loops; the only benchmark compares against NumPy, Octave, hmatrix and gonum
one_liner: Matlab-style vector and matrix library over Accelerate; a 2017 Swift 3 benchmark puts it near NumPy, with no Swift-loop baseline.

name: Apache Fory (Swift)
baseline: Codable with Foundation JSONEncoder / JSONDecoder (macOS 15.7.2); SwiftProtobuf also compared
one_liner: Macro-generated cross-language binary serializer; 11-59x the throughput of Codable JSON and up to 5.6x SwiftProtobuf in its own benchmark.

name: SwiftZSTD (zstd)
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB and NSData.compressed(using: .zlib)
one_liner: Swift wrapper for zstd; the codec compresses 4.7-15x and decompresses about 4x faster than zlib at similar or better ratios.

name: ane_transformers (Neural Engine Transformer reference)
baseline: Hugging Face distilbert converted to Core ML as-is
one_liner: Apple's PyTorch reference for Neural Engine-friendly Transformers; up to 10x faster than an as-is Core ML conversion of distilbert.

name: ml-stable-diffusion (Core ML Stable Diffusion, SPLIT_EINSUM_V2 attention)
baseline: The same Stable Diffusion Core ML model converted with the SPLIT_EINSUM attention implementation
one_liner: Apple's Core ML port of Stable Diffusion; its SPLIT_EINSUM_V2 attention is claimed 10-30% faster on iPhone and iPad Neural Engines.

name: swift-algorithms (min(count:), max(count:))
baseline: sorted().prefix(k) (sorting the whole collection to take the k smallest)
one_liner: Apple's partial selection: the k smallest or largest elements in about O(n) for small k instead of sorting everything.

name: swift-collections (Deque)
baseline: Swift Array used as a queue, inserting at the front with insert(_:at: 0) (capacity reserved up front)
one_liner: Apple's ring-buffer double-ended queue; constant-time prepend and popFirst where Array.insert(at: 0) and removeFirst are linear.

name: swift-collections (Heap)
baseline: Re-sorting an Array (or scanning it with min()/max()) to get the smallest or largest element
one_liner: Apple's array-backed min-max heap for priority queues; O(log n) push and pop instead of re-sorting an Array.

name: swift-collections (OrderedSet)
baseline: Swift Array used as a unique ordered list, checked with Array.contains before insert
one_liner: Apple's ordered hashed set: Array order with constant-time membership, replacing contains() scans over arrays.

name: swift-collections (TreeSet, TreeDictionary)
baseline: Swift Set and Dictionary when a copy is kept and then mutated (copy-on-write duplicates the whole hash table)
one_liner: Persistent hashed set and dictionary (CHAMP tries) that make mutating shared copies logarithmic instead of a full copy.

name: SwiftNIO (hand-written NIOHTTP1 server)
baseline: Vapor 4 (TechEmpower "vapor" implementation, same Swift toolchain and build flags)
one_liner: SwiftNIO used directly as a bare HTTP/1.1 server, measured at 4-11x Vapor's throughput on TechEmpower's trivial endpoints.

name: SwiftProtobuf (binary wire format)
baseline: Codable with Foundation JSONEncoder / JSONDecoder (swift-foundation, macOS 15.7.2)
one_liner: Apple's Protocol Buffers runtime for Swift; 5-19x the throughput of Codable JSON in a third-party benchmark, at about half the bytes.

name: WhisperKit (argmax-oss-swift)
baseline: Apple SpeechAnalyzer with the SpeechTranscriber model (iOS 26 / macOS 26); whisper.cpp with its Core ML encoder
one_liner: Whisper speech recognition in Swift on Core ML and the Neural Engine; faster than Apple's SpeechAnalyzer only with a less accurate model.

name: BTree (attaswift)
baseline: A sorted Swift Array kept in order with binary-search insertion
one_liner: In-memory B-tree giving sorted lists, sets and maps with O(log n) insert; beats a sorted Array only at large counts.

name: Bazel (with rules_swift, rules_apple and rules_xcodeproj)
baseline: xcodebuild / the Xcode build system with no remote cache
one_liner: Google's build system with Swift and Apple rules; Spotify cut iOS CI waits 4x, mostly through remote caching and remote execution.

name: GPUImage (OpenGL ES)
baseline: Core Image on iOS 5 for live camera filtering
one_liner: OpenGL ES filter framework that beat iOS 5 Core Image by 40x on an iPhone 4 and 4x on a 4S; unmaintained since 2016.

name: FastCoders (JSONDecoderEncoderBenchmarks)
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder / JSONEncoder (swift-foundation, before PR #1481) in an app with about 150k protocol conformances
one_liner: Patched JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder that skips slow conformance checks; 2x faster in a huge app, now largely merged into swift-foundation.

name: CocoaLumberjack
baseline: NSLog (ASL-backed, pre-2016) and print
one_liner: Logging framework that claimed an order-of-magnitude win over NSLog in 2010 benchmarks; untested against today's NSLog or os.Logger.

name: xcbeautify
baseline: xcpretty (Ruby xcodebuild output formatter)
one_liner: Swift replacement for xcpretty that formats xcodebuild output; claimed 2x faster, but never published a benchmark.

name: PugiSwift
baseline: XMLCoder (Codable over Foundation XMLParser) and Fuzi (libxml2)
one_liner: Swift macros over the pugixml C++ parser; 14x XMLCoder and 3.7x Fuzi on a 212 KB file in its author's test.

name: FLAnimatedImage
baseline: UIImage.animatedImage(with:duration:) or UIImageView animationImages holding every decoded frame
one_liner: GIF player that decodes frames just in time instead of holding all of them; its memory savings were never published as measurements.

name: llama.cpp (Metal backend on Apple silicon)
baseline: Core ML LLM conversions running on the Neural Engine (CoreML-LLM)
one_liner: C/C++ LLM runtime with a Metal backend; beats Core ML's Neural Engine path on burst decode but trails MLX Swift on Apple silicon.

name: GRDB.swift (records against Core Data)
baseline: Core Data (NSManagedObject fetch and insert on an SQLite store, default settings)
one_liner: SQLite toolkit for Swift whose record types fetched rows about 1.9x faster than Core Data in its own Release-build harness.

name: Hummingbird 1.x (HTTP server framework)
baseline: Vapor 4 (TechEmpower "vapor" implementation, same Swift toolchain and build flags)
one_liner: Hummingbird 1.x, a SwiftNIO web framework that served about twice Vapor's plaintext and JSON throughput in TechEmpower Round 23.

name: Hummingbird 2 (HTTP server framework)
baseline: Vapor 4 (TechEmpower "vapor" implementation, same Swift toolchain and build flags)
one_liner: Hummingbird 2, the async/await rewrite, which TechEmpower Round 23 measured as slower than Vapor on plaintext and JSON.

name: YYCache (YYMemoryCache, YYDiskCache)
baseline: NSCache, PINCache, and one-file-per-value disk caches
one_liner: Objective-C memory and SQLite-backed disk cache; 2015 charts show it ahead of NSCache and file caches, numbers chart-only.

name: IGListKit (IGListDiff)
baseline: Swift standard library difference(from:).inferringMoves() (CollectionDifference, Myers algorithm), Swift 5.1
one_liner: Instagram's list framework with a linear-time Heckel diff, measured 1.8-7.2x faster than the standard library's difference(from:).

name: SwiftXXHash (xxHash XXH3/XXH64)
baseline: Swift's Hasher (SipHash-1-3) and hashValue
one_liner: Swift wrapper for the official xxHash C library; XXH3 hashes bytes about 10x faster than SipHash in xxHash's x86 benchmark.

name: Dwifft
baseline: A naive diff implementation (README); today's default is the standard library's difference(from:)
one_liner: LCS-based diff with UIKit bindings; claims speed with no numbers and measured 7.6x slower than the stdlib diff.

name: Matft
baseline: NumPy 2.0.2 on the same Mac (the published comparison); no plain-Swift-loop baseline is published
one_liner: NumPy-style arrays for Swift on Accelerate; 10-33x faster than NumPy on sin and power, slower on sorting and comparisons.

name: Down
baseline: Markdown.pl (the original Perl implementation); no Swift parser measured
one_liner: Swift wrapper over cmark 0.29; its speed figures are cmark versus Markdown.pl and show no gain over Swift's cmark-based defaults.

name: Surge
baseline: Plain Swift loops over [Double] and [Float]
one_liner: Swift wrappers over Accelerate's vDSP, vForce and BLAS; claims near-Accelerate speed but publishes no numbers against plain loops.

name: Parse3339
baseline: Foundation DateFormatter and ISO8601DateFormatter
one_liner: Single-file RFC 3339 timestamp parser; parses in 16 ns with zero allocations, far ahead of Foundation formatters created per call.

name: Kitura (web framework)
baseline: Vapor 4 release candidate (TechEmpower "vapor" implementation; Fluent 4 RC with Postgres for the database test)
one_liner: Kitura, the IBM-started Swift web framework; TechEmpower Round 19 measured it at a third to half of Vapor's HTTP throughput.

name: CryptoSwift
baseline: CommonCrypto and CryptoKit
one_liner: Pure-Swift crypto algorithms; measured 3.5x to 57x slower than CommonCrypto, so use it for portability or missing algorithms, not speed.

name: FlexLayout (Yoga flexbox)
baseline: UIStackView (and Auto Layout) laying out self-sizing UICollectionView cells
one_liner: Swift wrapper over Meta's Yoga flexbox engine; about 4x faster than UIStackView on current iPhones in LayoutFrameworkBenchmark.

name: PinLayout
baseline: Auto Layout (NSLayoutConstraint) laying out self-sizing UICollectionView cells
one_liner: Frame-based layout DSL for UIKit that runs about 3x faster than Auto Layout on current iPhones in LayoutFrameworkBenchmark.

name: SwiftBitset
baseline: Foundation IndexSet
one_liner: Daniel Lemire's word-array bitset for integer sets; much faster than IndexSet on scattered values, slower at count.

name: SwiftWyhash (WyRand)
baseline: SystemRandomNumberGenerator via Double.random(in:)
one_liner: Pure-Swift wyrand generator; about 50x faster than Double.random(in:) with the system generator for bulk random arrays.

name: libjpeg-turbo (on iOS)
baseline: ImageIO JPEG decoding (Apple's AppleJPEG path) behind UIImage(data:)
one_liner: SIMD JPEG codec 2-6x faster than libjpeg, but measured no faster than ImageIO's AppleJPEG on iPhone.

name: Lighter (Enlighter-generated SQLite bindings)
baseline: GRDB and SQLite.swift decoding rows through Codable
one_liner: Code generator that binds SQLite statements directly to Swift structs; 6.6x faster than GRDB with Codable in an independent rerun.

name: LayoutKit
baseline: Auto Layout (NSLayoutConstraint) laying out self-sizing UICollectionView cells
one_liner: LinkedIn's immutable layout engine for UIKit; still about 3.8x faster than Auto Layout in a 2025 run, but archived since 2021.

name: lld (Mach-O port, ld64.lld)
baseline: ld64 in Xcode 14 and earlier; ld-prime is the default from Xcode 15
one_liner: LLVM's Mach-O linker: about 2x faster than Xcode 14's ld64, but slower than Xcode 15's ld-prime on Apple silicon.

name: MetalBlurHash
baseline: Wolt's reference BlurHash Swift encoder and decoder (CPU)
one_liner: Metal port of BlurHash; decodes a 3840 x 2560 placeholder 250x faster than Wolt's CPU code on an M1 Max.

name: CwlUtils (Xoshiro)
baseline: SystemRandomNumberGenerator, which calls arc4random_buf on Apple platforms
one_liner: Swift Xoshiro256** generator from CwlUtils; 69x faster than arc4random_buf, the source behind SystemRandomNumberGenerator.

name: swift-yyjson (YYJSON)
baseline: Foundation JSONSerialization.jsonObject (macOS 26, swift-foundation era)
one_liner: yyjson wrapper with JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder-style APIs; parses 9-15x faster than JSONSerialization, Codable path unmeasured.

name: Bodega (SQLiteStorageEngine)
baseline: One file per object on disk (Bodega's DiskStorageEngine, the plain FileManager write pattern)
one_liner: Key-value store whose SQLite engine loads 1,000 objects in about 0.1 s against 0.25 s for one-file-per-object storage.

name: ZippyJSON
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder before iOS 17 / macOS 14 (Swift wrapper over NSJSONSerialization)
one_liner: Drop-in JSONDecoder built on simdjson; 3-4x faster than the pre-iOS 17 decoder, and slower than iOS 17+'s by its own README.

name: zld
baseline: ld64 from Xcode 11-13
one_liner: Archived fork of ld64 that linked about 40% faster in 2020; lld and then Xcode 15's ld-prime overtook it.

name: MLX Swift (LLM decoding on the Apple silicon GPU)
baseline: Core ML LLM conversions running on the Neural Engine (CoreML-LLM), with llama.cpp's Metal backend as the other common choice
one_liner: Swift API for Apple's MLX array framework; decodes LLMs on the GPU faster than Core ML's Neural Engine path in short bursts.

name: SwiftFormat
baseline: swift-format (swiftlang/swift-format)
one_liner: Swift code formatter with its own tokenizer; timed 8x faster than swift-format on one small file in 2019, unmeasured since.

name: DeepDiff
baseline: Other Swift diffing libraries (Differ, Dwifft, Changeset, ListDiff); the standard library's difference(from:) did not exist yet
one_liner: Heckel-based Swift diff for table and collection views; faster than Myers libraries, but its own benchmark overstates the gap.

name: IkigaJSON (orlandos-nl/swift-json)
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder / JSONEncoder after the swift-foundation rewrite (macOS 26)
one_liner: SwiftNIO-friendly Codable JSON coder; its own 2026 benchmark puts it level with or behind modern Foundation, with fewer decode allocations.

name: Fast Image Cache
baseline: Loading individual JPEG files with UIImage(contentsOfFile:) and letting Core Animation decode them on the main thread
one_liner: Stores pre-decoded, byte-aligned thumbnails in memory-mapped image tables; 59 vs 35 FPS scrolling on iOS 7-era hardware.

name: SQLiteData (StructuredQueries decoding over GRDB)
baseline: SwiftData (the README's stated replacement target); measured only against GRDB and SQLite.swift
one_liner: SwiftData-style observation over SQLite; decodes rows 2.2x faster than GRDB's hand-written mapping, but has no published SwiftData numbers.

name: swift-parsing (UTF8View parsers vs Scanner)
baseline: Foundation Scanner and hand-written String.split parsing
one_liner: Composable parser library; its UTF-8 parsers beat Foundation Scanner 3x-9x, but Substring parsers do not beat hand-written split code.

name: swift-parsing (RFC 3339 date parser benchmark)
baseline: Foundation DateFormatter and ISO8601DateFormatter (cached instances, pre-2023 Foundation)
one_liner: Example RFC 3339 parser built with swift-parsing that ran 6.7x faster than a cached DateFormatter in a 2023 benchmark.

name: DifferenceKit
baseline: Swift standard library difference(from:).inferringMoves() (CollectionDifference, Myers algorithm), Swift 5.1
one_liner: Linear-time Heckel diff for table and collection views, measured 33-144x faster than the standard library's difference(from:).

name: RxSwift
baseline: Apple Combine (PassthroughSubject, map/filter, flatMap, combineLatest)
one_liner: Reactive Extensions for Swift; slower than Combine in 10 of 11 published operator benchmarks, so speed is not a reason to pick it.

name: Realm Swift
baseline: SwiftData (iOS 17) and Core Data
one_liner: Embedded object database with its own engine; 3-6x faster than SwiftData on large writes but over 10x slower on relationship queries.

name: SwiftLint (SwiftSyntax-based rules)
baseline: Earlier SwiftLint releases with SourceKit-based rules (0.48 and earlier)
one_liner: The standard Swift linter; rewriting rules on SwiftSyntax made them 7-10x faster and whole runs 6-30% faster per release.

name: ReerJSON
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder / JSONEncoder, both before iOS 17 and after the swift-foundation rewrite (iOS 26, macOS 15.6)
one_liner: yyjson-backed drop-in JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder; its charts show it ahead of Foundation on iOS 26, but the numbers are only in images.

name: Rive (rive-ios, vs Lottie)
baseline: lottie-ios with its Core Animation rendering engine (the iOS default since Lottie 4.0)
one_liner: Rive's iOS runtime draws vector animations with Metal; the faster-than-Lottie numbers in circulation come from Android, not iOS.

name: Chronicle
baseline: os_log / os.Logger, NSLog and print
one_liner: Experimental in-process structured logger claiming a few dozen nanoseconds per message; no published comparison with os_log or print.

name: unxip
baseline: xip(1) and Archive Utility (Apple's Bom) for extracting Xcode .xip files
one_liner: Swift tool that extracts Xcode .xip files about 2-3x faster than xip(1) and Archive Utility, per its author.

name: XCRemoteCache
baseline: xcodebuild / Xcode builds with no remote cache
one_liner: Spotify's remote cache for Xcode builds; cut median clean builds 70% at Spotify, but needs old driver settings and has stalled.

name: swift-extras-base64
baseline: Foundation base64EncodedString / Data(base64Encoded:) with Swift 5.3 (2020), macOS and Linux
one_liner: Foundation-free Base64 that was 3-10x faster than 2020 Foundation; its author has since brought the approach into Foundation.

name: swift-extras-json (ExtrasJSON, formerly pure-swift-json)
baseline: Foundation JSONEncoder / JSONDecoder in Swift 5.1 and 5.2 (macOS: pre-2023 NSJSONSerialization-backed; Linux: swift-corelibs-foundation before Swift 5.5)
one_liner: Foundation-free JSON coder that beat Swift 5.1/5.2 Foundation by 1.5-10x; its parsing approach later went into Foundation itself.

name: swift-foundation NewCodable (JSONDecodable + JSONParserDecoder, experimental)
baseline: Decodable + Foundation JSONDecoder (current swift-foundation)
one_liner: Apple's prototype successor to Codable for JSON; about 6x JSONDecoder's throughput on twitter.json, on an experimental branch.

name: SwiftPM prebuilt swift-syntax for macros
baseline: Building swift-syntax from source for every package that uses macros (SwiftPM and Xcode before the prebuilts)
one_liner: SwiftPM downloads a release-built swift-syntax for macros instead of compiling it, cutting minutes from clean builds.

name: MMKV
baseline: NSUserDefaults (UserDefaults.standard)
one_liner: mmap-backed key-value store from WeChat; much faster than NSUserDefaults for bulk writes in a vendor chart, on par for reads.

name: Texture (ASDisplayNode, ASCollectionNode)
baseline: Auto Layout and manual frame layout of UICollectionView cells on the main thread
one_liner: Node-based UI framework (ex-AsyncDisplayKit) that cut main-thread cell layout time 5.4x vs Auto Layout in an independent 2025 run.

name: Differ
baseline: Dwifft 0.x (O(n*m) longest-common-subsequence diff), as chosen by the README
one_liner: Myers O((N+M)D) diff with UIKit helpers; its speed claim is against early Dwifft, and the stdlib diff now beats it.

name: SWCompression
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB / NSData.compressed(using: .zlib), and Apple's LZ4
one_liner: Pure-Swift decompressors for Deflate, LZ4, LZMA, BZip2 and archive formats; roughly 23-74x slower than the C codecs.

name: Tuist (module cache)
baseline: xcodebuild clean build with no cache
one_liner: Xcode project generator whose module cache swaps unchanged targets for prebuilt binaries, cutting clean builds 2-3x in its benchmarks.

name: PostgresKit / PostgresNIO raw SQL (in Vapor)
baseline: Fluent ORM with fluent-postgres-driver (Model.find on req.db) in the same Vapor 4 app
one_liner: Raw parameterized SQL through PostgresKit in Vapor, measured at about 1.8-2.2x Fluent's throughput in TechEmpower Rounds 20 and 22.

name: SQLKit query builder (in Vapor, on PostgresKit)
baseline: Fluent ORM with fluent-postgres-driver (Model.find on req.db) in the same Vapor 4 app
one_liner: SQLKit's typed SQL builder in Vapor, measured at about 1.6-2.1x Fluent's throughput in TechEmpower Rounds 20 and 22.

name: ZIPFoundation
baseline: SSZipArchive (ZipArchive, minizip-based); the published test actually used macOS's zip/unzip command-line tools
one_liner: Pure-Swift ZIP library on Apple's libcompression; its 2017 charts show faster extraction than macOS unzip, with no SSZipArchive comparison.

name: swift-json-schema (generated SwiftJSON ObjectView decoding)
baseline: Foundation JSONDecoder after the swift-foundation rewrite (Apple M4 Max)
one_liner: Build plugin that generates structs plus zero-copy JSON initializers; 1.5-2x faster than JSONDecoder on small inputs, slower on large ones.

name: xcodes (aria2 downloads)
baseline: Single-connection URLSession download of Xcode (xcodes without aria2, or a browser download)
one_liner: Command-line Xcode installer that downloads over up to 16 connections with aria2, claimed 3-5x faster than URLSession.
